title: Proteomics of a murine bronchoalveolar lavage sample, LC-MSMS
projectDescription: This study evaluates the performance of adapted SPEED (Sample Preparation by Easy Extraction and Digestion) protocols, a simplified, detergent-free approach tailored for various biological matrices, including lysis-resistant samples. All datasets can be found searching for the keyword NKUAProt001.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid samples underwent protein precipitation using four methods: ethanol, acetonitrile (MeCN), acetone, and the single-pot, solid-phase-enhanced sample preparation (SP3) method. Protein concentration was measured using the Bradford assay, and 5 μg of protein was precipitated at 4C using six volumes of either acetone, MeCN, or ethanol, followed by centrifugation at 18,200 RCF. SP3 precipitation involved magnetic beads combined with MeCN, followed by washing and elution steps. Reduction and alkylation were performed using TCEP/CAA, followed by trypsin digestion. Peptides were purified using C18 stage tips before LC-MS/MS analysis. Stage tips were conditioned with 250 μL of MeCN, 250 μL of solvent B (40% MeCN with 0.5% acetic acid) followed by 250 μL of solvent A (H₂O with 0.5% acetic acid). Peptides were loaded and washed with solvent A, and final elution was performed with 40 μL of solvent B, then dried, reconstituted in solvent A, and injected for LC-MS/MS analysis.
dataProcessingProtocol: The raw data were analyzed using FragPipe v22.0,  using quantification with DIA-NN v1.9.0, in library-free mode. DIA-Tracer was used to enhance feature alignment and quantification consistency across runs. The search included a tolerance for up to four missed cleavages, peptide length ranging from 5 to 30 amino acids and peptide mass ranging from 300 to 5,000 Da. The false discovery rate (FDR) was set to 1%. Data were queried against UP000007604.
